7	
8	Stated by Filip 2026-08-31. When the overlay shows a corner swap (Roy carrying
9	the red box), he selects **red** and logs the punch — i.e. he picks the
10	rectangle around the fighter who threw it, not the fighter named red at upload.
11	
12	So `label_events.corner` and `fighter_frames.corner` are **the same pointer**:
13	both name a track slot, not a person. Inside a `corner_swap` span they are both
14	"wrong" about the name and consistent about the human. The Stage 2 join
15	`label_events(F, corner) -> fighter_frames(F, corner) -> keypoints` therefore
16	already yields correct training rows with nothing applied.
17	
18	**Why:** it inverts the design in the plan. Applying the swap at export — as
19	`ai/eval/schema.py:152` ("Applied at export time when joining labels to
20	fighter_frames.keypoints") and `plan/02c-labelling-ui.md:156` ("flips red/blue
21	in the exported training tensor") both instruct — would attach the label to the
22	*other* fighter's skeleton. That is the exact silent corruption
23	`plan/02a-upload-tracks.md:95` set out to prevent, caused by the mitigation.
24	The premise there was identity-labelling; the actual convention is
25	box-labelling, under which the corruption never existed.
26	
27	**How to apply:** never apply `corner_swaps` to a label-to-keypoint join. Apply
28	it only where a *person* is needed (per-fighter stats, `fight_events.fighter_id`),
29	and at read time — mutating `fighter_frames.corner` would desync it from
30	`label_events.corner` and break the join that currently works. Two knock-ons:
31	`score.py:225`'s "fighter attribution %" is circular (the labeller read the
32	corner off the pipeline's own overlay, so it can never detect a swap — cf.
33	[[fight-ai-eval-labels-are-circular]]); and span *boundary* error no longer
34	corrupts training data as `plan/02d-label-quality.md:213` claims, though
35	detection rate still matters for the tracker metric. The spans remain the
36	ground truth for [[tracker-swaps-at-cuts-and-clinches]], which is now their
37	main purpose. See also [[corner-accuracy-blind-on-ground]].
38

11	Measured 2026-08-30 against the labeller's own `label_spans` of kind
12	`corner_swap` — these are the ground truth for identity swaps and need no
13	re-run to use. Fight 54 has 8 spans (6–35 s each), fight 52 has 5 (1.7–8.7 s).
14	
15	Against a 5000-frame random control per fight, window ±6 frames:
16	- **fight 54 span STARTS**: 4/8 in the top decile of frame-to-frame box jump
17	  (chance 1.5) — a camera switch.
18	- **fight 54 span ENDS**: 4/7 in the top decile of inter-fighter box IoU
19	  (chance 1.5).
20	- **fight 52 span STARTS**: median inter-fighter IoU 0.73 vs control 0.00 — a
21	  clinch.
22	
23	Both entry points are where `FighterTracker`'s geometry-only cost is
24	uninformative. n is small (5 and 8 spans), so treat this as directional.
25	
26	Two structural facts behind it: nothing in `ai/` detects a shot boundary at all
27	(grep for cut/shot/scene finds only prose), and `FighterTracker._assign` has **no
28	maximum-cost gate** — only the Hungarian padding cells carry the 1e6 sentinel, so
29	a detection anywhere in the frame will always match some slot rather than letting
30	the slot coast.
31	
32	A global HSV-histogram cut detector is the wrong instrument here: it found only
33	29 cuts in 47k frames of fight 54, because broadcast MMA cuts between cameras
34	pointed at the same cage barely change the global histogram. Use the geometric
35	signal (simultaneous box jump) instead.
36	
37	**Why:** a swap that enters at a cut persists until the next one, because
38	`assign_corners` can only apply a global flip — see
39	[[corner-hysteresis-cannot-fix-swaps]].
40	
41	**How to apply:** measure any tracking change against these spans rather than by
42	eye, and check the run log first — on fight 54 the appearance path was skipped
43	entirely (`ambiguous tape (both slots read blue)`), so the static legacy map ran
44	and no swap was corrected at all.

2	name: corner-hysteresis-cannot-fix-swaps
3	description: "assign_corners' hysteresis barrier is charged twice, so a tracker identity swap is mathematically uncorrectable without visible glove tape."
4	metadata: 
5	  node_type: memory
6	  type: project
7	  originSessionId: fbf2c258-92a1-4a58-8ba1-d5ff99286f32
8	  modified: 2026-08-30T09:58:15.667Z

10	
11	Measured 2026-08-30. In `assign_corners._assign_frame_labels`, `_cost` adds
12	`CORNER_HYSTERESIS_WEIGHT` (0.5) per detection whose label would flip. A corner
13	swap always flips both slots, so the barrier is **1.0**. Evidence per detection
14	is `CORNER_TAPE_WEIGHT` (0.6) × tape + `CORNER_HIST_WEIGHT` (0.4) × hist, and
15	when no glove tape is visible `_tape_distance_term` returns exactly 0.5 for both
16	corners (confidence factor 0), so the tape term cancels. Torso histogram alone
17	can therefore move the two-detection total by at most **0.8 < 1.0**: the flip
18	can never win. In practice Bhattacharyya gaps give ~0.16–0.32, versus a 1.0
19	barrier.
20	
21	The single-detection branch charges the barrier only **once** (0.5), so a
22	one-sided observation faces a *lower* bar than both fighters seen together —
23	backwards, since it is the weaker evidence.
24	
25	**Why:** this is the only mechanism that can repair a `FighterTracker` identity
26	swap, and it is disabled exactly when the gloves aren't visible — which is most
27	of a clinch and most of a ground sequence.
28	
29	**How to apply:** charge the barrier once per *mapping* decision (it is a
30	bijection — see the atomic-commit note already in ai/CLAUDE.md), consistently in
31	both branches, before touching the constant's value. Note the deeper issue too:
32	the mapping is global, so it cannot represent a swap that lasts only from one
33	camera cut to the next, and the run logs show it flip-flopping 444–813 times per
34	fight chasing local errors with a global boolean. See
35	[[tracker-swaps-at-cuts-and-clinches]] and
36	[[fight-ai-tracking-rewrite-plan]].

from datetime import datetime
from typing import Optional

from sqlalchemy import Boolean, Column, ForeignKey, Integer, String, Text, TIMESTAMP, text
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, model_validator

from app.utils.db import Base

EVENT_KINDS = ("point", "round", "corner_swap", "excluded")


class FightEvent(Base):
    __tablename__ = "fight_events"

    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True, index=True)
    fight_id = Column(Integer, ForeignKey("fights.id", ondelete="CASCADE"), nullable=False)
    source = Column(String(20), nullable=False)
    kind = Column(String(20), nullable=False)
    frame = Column(Integer, nullable=False)
    end_frame = Column(Integer, nullable=True)
    description = Column(Text, nullable=True)
    fighter_id = Column(Integer, ForeignKey("fighters.id", ondelete="SET NULL"), nullable=True)
    corner = Column(Integer, nullable=True)
    action = Column(String(50), nullable=True)
    target = Column(String(10), nullable=True)
    success = Column(Boolean, nullable=True)
    state = Column(String(20), nullable=True)
    value = Column(String(200), nullable=True)
    labeler = Column(String(100), nullable=True)
    created_at = Column(TIMESTAMP, nullable=False, server_default=text("CURRENT_TIMESTAMP"))
    is_verified = Column(Boolean, nullable=True)


class FightEventResponse(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(from_attributes=True)

    id: int
    fight_id: int
    source: str
    kind: str
    frame: int
    end_frame: Optional[int]
    description: Optional[str]
    fighter_id: Optional[int]
    corner: Optional[int]
    action: Optional[str]
    target: Optional[str]
    success: Optional[bool]
    state: Optional[str]
    value: Optional[str]
    labeler: Optional[str]
    created_at: datetime
    is_verified: Optional[bool]


class FightEventCreate(BaseModel):
    """The Annotate frontend's only write shape. `source` is deliberately not
    a field here — the service always writes `source="label"`, since this is
    exclusively Annotate's write path (the AI pipeline writes predictions via
    its own raw SQL, never through this schema). That makes it structurally
    impossible for a client request to spoof a prediction row."""

    kind: str = "point"
    frame: int
    end_frame: Optional[int] = None
    description: Optional[str] = None
    corner: Optional[int] = None
    action: Optional[str] = None
    target: Optional[str] = None
    success: Optional[bool] = None
    labeler: Optional[str] = None
    value: Optional[str] = None

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _validate_shape(self) -> "FightEventCreate":
        if self.kind not in EVENT_KINDS:
            raise ValueError(f"kind must be one of {EVENT_KINDS}")
        # fight_end is the one action with no structured way to reconstruct
        # its text (winner/method/detail aren't columns) — everything else is
        # rebuilt on demand client-side from action/target/corner, so storing
        # it would just go stale the next time a corner_swap span is edited.
        if self.kind == "point" and self.action == "fight_end" and not self.description:
            raise ValueError("description is required for a fight_end event")
        if self.corner is not None and self.corner not in (0, 1):
            raise ValueError("corner must be 0 (red) or 1 (blue)")
        if self.action and self.action.startswith("state_") and self.corner is not None:
            raise ValueError("corner must be null for a state_* action — a fight state isn't scoped to a corner")
        return self


class FightEventUpdate(BaseModel):
    """Range (round/corner_swap/excluded) edits only — point events are
    create+delete-only, same as label_events always was."""

    frame: Optional[int] = None
    end_frame: Optional[int] = None
    value: Optional[str] = None


class FightEventVerify(BaseModel):
    """Training Data QA's only write shape. `is_verified` is a tri-state:
    True (confirmed training-worthy), False (declined), or None (back to
    pending) — always required in the payload so "clear the verdict" is a
    real, explicit request rather than an omitted field."""

    is_verified: Optional[bool]

This already works — I verified it live rather than just reading the code.

I loaded [fight 44](http://localhost:5173/fights/44) (Nazhand vs. Staropoli), which has a hand-labelled `corner_swap` span from frame 2647–6877. Inside that span there's a labelled `cross` at frame 2840 with `corner=1` (the blue box). Seeking the player to that frame, the live feed shows:

> **NAZHAND cross to the head** — #2840

Nazhand is the *red*-corner fighter, so the blue-box label is correctly flipped to red for display, exactly like your example.

This is already implemented end-to-end and was committed in a prior session (not part of your current uncommitted diff):

- [cornerSwap.ts](frontend/src/utils/cornerSwap.ts) — `isFrameSwapped(frame, spans)`, shared logic for "is this frame inside a confirmed/open `corner_swap` span."
- [describeEvent.ts:38-42](frontend/src/utils/describeEvent.ts:38) — `nameForCorner` flips `corner` (`1 - corner`) when `ctx.swapped` is true, before resolving to the red/blue fighter name.
- [LiveFeed.tsx:52-55](frontend/src/components/player/LiveFeed.tsx:52) — computes `swapped: isFrameSwapped(e.frame, cornerSwapSpans ?? [])` per event and passes it into `describeEvent`.
- [Player.tsx:56-60](frontend/src/pages/Player.tsx:56) — fetches `corner_swap` spans (always `source='label'`, even for an `ai_labeled` fight) and threads them into both `LiveFeed` and `FighterOverlay`.
- [FighterOverlay.tsx:107-111](frontend/src/components/FighterOverlay.tsx:107) — same flip applied to the box/skeleton color so the video overlay agrees with the feed text.

Nothing in the underlying `corner` column is mutated — the flip is display-only and recomputed on every render, so editing a `corner_swap` span later updates already-logged events immediately (matches [[label-events-corner-is-box-not-person]]).

One caveat worth flagging: the FIGHT STATISTICS panel (strike counts by target/position) does **not** apply this correction — `liveStats.ts` attributes by raw `corner`/`fighter_id`, so a strike inside a swap span is currently counted for the wrong fighter's tally even though the feed text shows it correctly. Let me know if you want that fixed too — it's a separate code path from what you described.

content.text:
Confirmed — this is a real mislabel, not the code you asked about last time. Here's what I found, verified against the actual footage.

**Fight 42 has zero `corner_swap` spans logged**, unlike fight 44. So the swap-correction feature from before has nothing to apply here — it's not misfiring, there's just no data telling it to fire.

**The label itself is wrong.** I overlaid the tracker's actual bounding boxes on the video at frame 1168 (the `cross`, logged with `corner=0`):

- `corner=0`'s box lands squarely on the **blue-shorts** fighter (the one extending the punch)
- `corner=1`'s box lands on the **red-shorts** fighter (the one covering up)

Since `corner=0` always renders as the red-roster name (Milidragovic) and `corner=1` as blue (Moosman), the feed shows "Milidragovic cross" for a punch the blue-shorts fighter — Moosman — actually threw. That matches what you saw.

**Where it went wrong:** scanning the tracker data for frame-to-frame jumps (the same signature from the [[tracker-swaps-at-cuts-and-clinches]] research), I found the two fighters' boxes merge into nearly the same position at frame ~1010 (a clinch), and when they separate one frame later, `corner=1`'s box teleports from x≈536 to x≈1148 while `corner=0` continues smoothly — a textbook clinch-entry identity swap. Every one of fight 42's 16 labelled strikes/events falls after frame 1011, so if this swap was never corrected later in the fight, **all of them** could be attributed backward, not just this one cross.

This is a labelling gap, not a bug: the display-correction code is doing exactly what it did for fight 44 — it just has no span to work from here, because fight 42 was apparently never reviewed for corner swaps in Annotate.

How do you want to handle it?
